workingTitle: XRISM finds where iron hides in a dense Galactic sightline
publicationStatus: Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal
coreFacts: XRISM observed the bright X-ray binary GX 340+0 twice for a combined exposure of about 305 kiloseconds.
Resolve measured absorption around the iron K-edge near 7.1 keV along a dense Milky Way sightline.
The best-fit model places about 95 percent of the iron in dust rather than gas.
Of the solid-phase iron, the model assigns about 38 percent to metallic iron, 47 percent to iron sulfides, and the remainder to silicates.
caveats: This is a pilot study of one high-column-density sightline.
The mineral fractions are inferred by comparing the spectrum with laboratory-based dust models.
The authors say the result may indicate that metallic iron and iron sulfides matter more in dense sightlines than in diffuse interstellar space.
